persona.role: maths PhD student in number theory

sent_to_model:
Hi, need help with a LinkedIn post. Our student-run winter school on elliptic curves got over on Saturday and I was one of the 3 organisers, so I have to put up the thank you post on behalf of the team. My guide and other faculty will see it, also the speakers and many people from other departments. Want to thank everyone by name and also mention some numbers so people know it was a serious event and not just a picnic. Also want to say we will do it again next year if funding comes. Names, numbers etc below. Keep it to 360-400 words and within 3,000 characters including spaces so I can post it. Please include the plan for sharing slides and sheets too.

- Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms, 5-7 Nov 2026, Seminar Hall 2, Dept of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune
- 41 participants (MSc + early PhD) from 9 states, 112 applications came, selected on statement + one reference
- organisers me, Ketaki Joglekar, Faizan Mirza; faculty mentor Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan
- speakers Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) on Mordell-Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) on modular forms, Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki online from Kraków on computations in Sage
- funding Rs 2.4 lakh from institute student initiative grant, covered hostel stay + travel for 18 outstation students
- day 2 afternoon power went for nearly 2 hrs, laptops died, we shifted problem session to canteen with 2 rolling whiteboards, actually best session of the three days
- one MSc student from Silchar found an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes, she corrected it live and thanked him
- office staff Mr. Prakash Salunke sorted hostel rooms at 11pm when the booking got messed up
- small schools like this matter more than big conferences for MSc people, they get to actually ask questions
- problem sessions run by PhD students worked well, should keep that format
- thank speakers, mentor, staff, volunteers (6 PhD students did TA work), participants
- say we hope to run second edition in late 2027, depends on grant
- slides and problem sheets will go on dept website in 2 weeks, mention that

(About me: maths PhD student in number theory, 27, Pune, India. Length: it should come to 360-400 words, and no more than 3,000 characters.)

must_cover: Thanks the named organisers, speakers, mentor and office staff as well as volunteers and participants.
Includes some supplied numerical facts to convey the scale or support of the event.
Says slides and problem sheets will be posted on the department website within two weeks.
Says the team hopes to run a second edition in late 2027, subject to grant funding.
